lean_claims.says: Advances are applied automatically: a party never has an open bill and an unapplied advance at the same time.
lean_claims.doc: Advances are applied automatically: a party never has an open bill and an unapplied advance at the same time.
lean_claims.lean:
def advancesAlwaysApplied : Prop :=
  ∀ (ops : List Op) (q : Nat), openBills (run ops) q = [] ∨ advances (run ops) q = []

lean_claims.says: A running balance kept per party always equals the balance worked out from the facts, through bills, payments and reversals.
lean_claims.doc: The running balance always equals the balance worked out from the facts.
lean_claims.lean:
def cachedBalanceAgrees : Prop :=
  ∀ (ops : List Op) (q : Nat), (run ops).cache q = balance (run ops) q

lean_claims.says: Reading only the first k open bills does NOT settle like reading all of them (a concrete counterexample).
Settlement pays oldest first: a bill receives anything only if every bill before it in the order is paid in full.
lean_claims.doc: Oldest first: a bill receives anything only if every bill before it in the order is paid in full.
lean_claims.lean:
def matchPaysOldestFirst : Prop :=
  ∀ (owed adv : List (Nat × Int)), wellFormed owed → wellFormed adv →
    ∀ (i j : Nat) (hi : i < owed.length) (hj : j < owed.length), i < j →
      0 < paidTo (matchUp owed adv) owed[j].1 → paidTo (matchUp owed adv) owed[i].1 = owed[i].2

lean_claims.says: Settlement settles as much as possible: the total applied is the smaller of everything owed and every advance. (Allocating nothing does not satisfy this.)
lean_claims.doc: As much debt as possible is settled: the total matched is the smaller of everything owed and every advance. (Allocating nothing does not satisfy this.)

lean_claims.says: Settlement never pays a bill more than it owes or takes more from a payment than its advance, and every allocation is positive and names an offered bill and payment.
lean_claims.doc: Every allocation is positive, goes to an offered bill from an offered payment, and no bill or payment receives or gives more than offered.
lean_claims.lean:
def matchWithinLimits : Prop :=
  ∀ (owed adv : List (Nat × Int)), wellFormed owed → wellFormed adv →
    (∀ x ∈ matchUp owed adv, 0 < x.amount ∧ x.bill ∈ owed.map (·.1) ∧ x.payment ∈ adv.map (·.1)) ∧
    (∀ b ∈ owed, paidTo (matchUp owed adv) b.1 ≤ b.2) ∧
    (∀ p ∈ adv, takenFrom (matchUp owed adv) p.1 ≤ p.2)

lean_claims.says: No payment is ever applied beyond its amount.
lean_claims.doc: No payment is ever applied beyond its amount.

lean_claims.says: No bill is ever settled beyond what it owes, and none is ever owed more than its amount.
lean_claims.doc: No bill is ever settled beyond what it owes, and none is owed more than its amount.

lean_claims.says: An operation about one party changes nothing about any other party: not its bills, what they owe, its payments, their advances, or its balance.
lean_claims.doc: Parties are isolated: an operation about one party changes nothing about any other party.

lean_claims.says: In every state the ledger can reach: ids are unique, increasing and below the next id; every amount is positive; every allocation is positive and links a recorded bill and payment of the same party.
lean_claims.doc: Ids are unique, increasing in recording order and below the next id; every bill and payment amount is positive; every allocation is positive and refers to a recorded bill and payment of the same party.
lean_claims.lean:
def reachableInvariants : Prop :=
  ∀ (ops : List Op), let s := run ops
    (s.bills.map (·.id)).Pairwise (· < ·) ∧ (∀ b ∈ s.bills, b.id < s.nextBill ∧ 0 < b.amount) ∧
    (s.payments.map (·.id)).Pairwise (· < ·) ∧ (∀ p ∈ s.payments, p.id < s.nextPayment ∧ 0 < p.amount) ∧
    (∀ a ∈ s.allocs, 0 < a.amount ∧ ∃ b ∈ s.bills, ∃ p ∈ s.payments, b.id = a.bill ∧ p.id = a.payment ∧ b.party = p.party)

lean_claims.says: A bill or payment of zero or a negative amount is rejected and changes nothing.
lean_claims.doc: Bills and payments must be positive; anything else is rejected and changes nothing.
lean_claims.lean:
def rejectsNonPositive : Prop :=
  ∀ (s : State) (q d : Nat) (a : Int), a ≤ 0 → step s (.bill q d a) = s ∧ step s (.pay q a) = s

lean_claims.says: Reversing a live payment raises its party's balance by exactly its amount and changes no other party's balance.
lean_claims.doc: Reversing a live payment raises its party's balance by exactly its amount, and changes no other party's balance.
lean_claims.lean:
def reversalRestoresBalance : Prop :=
  ∀ (ops : List Op) (p : Payment), p ∈ (run ops).payments → p.reversed = false →
    balance (run (ops ++ [.reverse p.id])) p.party = balance (run ops) p.party + p.amount ∧
    ∀ q, q ≠ p.party → balance (run (ops ++ [.reverse p.id])) q = balance (run ops) q

lean_claims.says: Open bills are always in a fixed order, oldest date first with ties broken by bill id, so the same data always settles the same way (KT bug pattern 4).
lean_claims.doc: Bills are always settled in a fixed order: oldest date first, ties broken by bill id, so the same data always settles the same way (KT bug pattern 4).
lean_claims.lean:
def settlesOldestFirst : Prop :=
  ∀ (ops : List Op) (q : Nat), (openBills (run ops) q).Pairwise fun a b => billBefore a b = true

lean_claims.says: Every view of a balance agrees: billed minus paid equals what the bills still owe minus the unapplied advances (KT bug pattern 3).
lean_claims.doc: Every view of a balance agrees: billed minus paid equals what the bills still owe minus what the payments have left as advances (KT bug pattern 3).
lean_claims.lean:
def viewsAgree : Prop :=
  ∀ (ops : List Op) (q : Nat),
    balance (run ops) q =
      (((run ops).bills.filter (·.party == q)).map (outstanding (run ops))).sum
        - (((run ops).payments.filter (·.party == q)).map (advance (run ops))).sum

optimisations.title: Store a running balance per party instead of summing rows
optimisations.agent_says: Keep parties.balance up to date on every bill and payment, in the same transaction; reads become one row lookup.

compensated_by.lean:
def cachedBalanceAgrees : Prop :=
  ∀ (ops : List Op) (q : Nat), (run ops).cache q = balance (run ops) q

optimisations.title: Read at most 20 open bills when settling a payment
optimisations.agent_says: Payments are rarely larger than 20 bills, so LIMIT 20 on the open-bill query is safe and avoids long scans.

compensated_by.lean:
def cappedMatchAgrees : Prop :=
  ∀ (k : Nat) (bills advs : List (Nat × Int)), matchUpCapped k bills advs = matchUp bills advs

optimisations.title: Index bills(party_id, id) and payments(party_id)
optimisations.agent_says: Balance sums and oldest-first settlement scan every bill; an index on party avoids the scan and the sort. Indexes never change results.

optimisations.title: Keep one SQLite connection per server thread instead of one per request
optimisations.agent_says: Opening a connection and setting pragmas on every request is wasted work; results are unchanged.

optimisations.title: WAL with synchronous=NORMAL
optimisations.agent_says: Widely recommended: WAL is always consistent with synchronous=NORMAL, and it is much faster.

optimisations.title: WAL journal, keeping synchronous=EXTRA (same as FULL in WAL)
optimisations.agent_says: WAL commits need fewer syncs than a rollback journal and stay durable at FULL or above.
